paragraphs.text: Chrome extension and local companion that let an exact DeepSeek Harness session operate the tabs you
choose, in your own signed-in Chrome. Local-first. Unofficial, by Corsen AI.
# DeepSeek Harness Connector
**Use DeepSeek Harness in the Chrome you already use — with your existing logins — while controlling
exactly which tabs each session may touch.**
You pick a DeepSeek Harness session. You pick the tabs it may operate. That session can read and act
in those tabs, and in nothing else. Every other tab, and every other session, is out of reach.

No headless copy of your browser. No cookie reading. No cloud relay. Nothing leaves your machine
exc
ept what your own DeepSeek Harness sends to the model provider you configured.
> An unofficial community project by **Corsen AI**. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or certified b

> DeepSeek.
## Status

**0.1.0.** The routing core, the transport, the DeepSeek Harness plugin, the
Chrome extension with a

ll twenty-one browser actions, the installers, and the release packaging work
end to end and are cov

ered by 392 tests: 298 unit and protocol tests, 17 cases running the shipped
page module in a real C

hrome, and 77 real-browser end-to-end cases — multi-session isolation, a
page built to leak hidden c

ontent, a page built to give a model instructions, an attached tab that
changes origin mid-task, rec

overy from a killed service worker, a restarted broker, a replaced
agent connection, a closed tab an

d a relaunched Chrome, the released pair installed into a real
`dsh` with its broker killed and rest

arted as a process, DeepSeek Harness's own compatibility rule
and display-metadata reader run agains

t the installed package, and three live turns of a real
`dsh` process whose model — DeepSeek Harness

's own scripted mock provider — calls
`browser_snapshot` and `browser_screenshot` on the attached ta

b (the screenshot reaching a vision
model as pixels and a text-only model as DeepSeek Harness's plac

eholder), a real `dsh` process
starting the packaged broker it found missing, the panel's setup card

against a real broker, a
silent port and another program, and web components read and clicked throu
gh open shadow roots.

**Tested with DeepSeek Harness 0.1.2-rc.1, 0.1.5-rc.2, 0.2.1-rc.5 (npm `latest`) and 0.2.2-rc.1
(npm

`next`)**, on Linux, macOS and Windows; see `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md`
for the evidence per version an

d platform. The release artifacts build byte-identically on the

## What it does
| **Reads a page** | `browser_snapshot` returns the page as structured text: title, URL, visible tex
t, and a numbered inventory of controls the model can address. Text-first — no vision required — and
`browser_screenshot` adds the pixels, through DeepSeek Harness's own attachment service, when the m

odel can see. |
| **Acts on a page** | Click, type, press keys, scroll, hover, choose options, drag,
find text, and navigate in the tab you attached, addressed by references from the latest snapshot.

A session can also open, list, switch, and close its own tabs — and only its own. |
| **Keeps sessio
ns apart** | Each DeepSeek Harness session owns its own set of tabs. Two sessions running at once ne

ver see each other's pages. |
| **Fails closed** | A session with no attached tab gets a clear refus

al and nothing happens. There is no fallback to "whatever tab is active". |
| **Masks secrets** | Pa
sswords, one-time codes, payment fields, and hidden inputs are masked in the page, before anything l
eaves the browser. Masking follows the control, not one field: a masked textarea’s content stays out
of the page text, and a masked menu’s options are not listed. Credential-bearing URL parameters are
t, and a masked menu’s options are not listed. Credential-bearing URL parameters are scrubbed too. |
## What it does not do yet

DeepSeek Harness Desktop keeps its own `desktop` profile; installing there
(`dsh plugin --profile de

sktop add …`, with Desktop opened once and then quit) has not been tested
yet, and is not claimed.

Content inside iframes is neither read nor acted on: the page code runs in the tab's top document
an

d does not descend into frames. (Open shadow DOM — web components, most design systems — is
read and

acted on as the user sees it, through slots and nested roots; a closed shadow root cannot
be reache

d by any script and is not claimed.) There is no trusted-input mode
(`chrome.debugger`) for sites th

at ignore synthetic events — ADR 0006 keeps it out of this version
on purpose, and says what adding

hetic events — ADR 0006 keeps it out of this version
on purpose, and says what adding it would cost.
## What it never does
- **Never reads your cookies.** The extension does not request the `cookies` permission. Your logins

are preserved by operating the page you already have open, not by taking your credentials.
- **Neve

r uses the debugger.** No `chrome.debugger`, so no debugging banner on your tabs and no
scary instal

l warning. See ADR 0006.
- **Never sends anything to Corsen AI.** No analytics, no telemetry, no rel

ay, no crash reporting.
- **Never reads page content from, or acts in, a tab you did not attach.** E

xplicitly, per
session. The one thing it learns about other tabs is their title and URL, read locall

y when you
open the tab chooser so you can pick one, and never sent to DeepSeek Harness.

Page content does travel from the tab you attached, through the local connector, to your DeepSeek
Ha

rness — and from there to whichever model provider your DeepSeek Harness is configured to use. If
th
at provider is remote, the content reaches it. The connector adds no destination of its own.
## Security

- The broker binds loopback only, and refuses to start on any other address.
- Both sides prove know

ledge of a shared pairing code with a role-bound HMAC over a fresh nonce. The
code itself never cros

ses the wire. A proof captured from the browser cannot be replayed as the
agent, and a proof cannot

be replayed at all.
- The broker proves itself back, so a process squatting on the port cannot harve

st your pages.
- Ownership is checked before the action **and again when the result returns**, so a

tab that moves
between sessions mid-action cannot deliver its content to the wrong one.
- Page conte

nt is treated as untrusted throughout. A page cannot change settings, attach tabs, move
ownership, o
r reach the pairing code.

Details in `docs/SECURITY-MODEL.md` and
`docs/THREAT-MODEL.md`.
